references.text: John 6:29 refers to the prophecy about a prophet whom God will raise up, and whom the people must listen to. Jesus points out that faith in him is God's work, since he is the one sent by God.
Here Jesus expresses that he is the one sent by God, and that believing in him is crucial. This is a direct parallel to 6:29, where faith in the sent one is defined as God's work.
In this prayer, Jesus defines faith in him, the sent one, as the mark of eternal life. This corresponds with 6:29, where faith in the sent one is God's work.
Jesus emphasizes that believing in him is to believe in the one who sent him. This is a direct extension of the principle in 6:29 that faith in the sent one is God's work.
